summary: The import keeps the child-facing contract. A tap in the reader plays the clip of that word, a word with no clip is not a tap target, the song of w01 keeps its lead-in of 3 s, and the songs of w02 to w07 stay audio-only with a lead-in of 0. The phase changed data only: the 11 phase commits touch the eight week files, source.json, nine test files and plan.md. The interface Thai drafts are unchanged, no teacher screen shows a clip key, and no share field of w01 or w08 reaches a child or a parent. Three findings stay open as nonblocking. F1 is now a planned task: the PM decided at 14:2x that w02 to w07 stay draft because Workbooks owns meta.status, and that look P3 gains the tasks 3.5 and 3.6 with a review-only switch STORYTIME_REVIEW_DRAFT_WEEKS=1 that opens draft weeks in the local review environment only. F2 is a latent gap in the tap normalizer. F3 is data that no screen plays.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Major] apps/storytime/content/l2/w02.json to w07.json: the six weeks hold meta.status draft, so apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/page.tsx line 263 answers 404 for them, and apps/storytime/lib/readiness.ts line 95 blocks a week that is not published. Rationale: the phase changed no meta.status, so the import is clean. The PM decided at 14:2x that w02 to w07 stay draft because Workbooks owns meta.status, and that look P3 gains the tasks 3.5 and 3.6 with a review-only switch STORYTIME_REVIEW_DRAFT_WEEKS=1 that opens draft weeks in the local review environment only. The fact is therefore a planned task, not a blocker of this review. The clip files also stay outside the media bucket until task 3.4 runs, so the switch must also point the media base at the hand-off folder for the taps to sound.

F2 [Minor] apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/reader.tsx line 368: the tap normalizer is toLowerCase only, and it does not apply the K2 form that apps/storytime/__tests__/look-r3-import.test.ts lines 104 to 110 enforce on the keys. Rationale: a page word with a curly apostrophe or with trailing punctuation would be a visible tap target whose key lookup misses, because the key of the clip holds the straight apostrophe and no outer punctuation. The phase did not introduce this normalizer, and the reader code comes from Phase 1 task 1.10. A parsed scan of the seven imported week files returns 0 clip keys with an apostrophe, 0 timed words with a character outside a-z and 0 display words that fail to match their audio word, so no child sees a broken tap today. The gap appears when a later week adds such a word.

F3 [Minor] apps/storytime/content/l2/w01.json line 1330: the decodable book holds 11 clip keys, and no app file reads the clip map of the decodable book. Rationale: the decodable word tap still cuts the sentence recording at apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/decodable.tsx line 501, so the vowel-link defect of the 'a nurse' pair stays on the decodable page. The phase introduced the data, and the decodable behaviour is pre-existing from Phase 1 and Phase 2. The decodable page sits outside the Phase 3 acceptance, so no phase gate fails.
